title: WizardDialog
wrapsNative: sheet(isPresented:) holding a NavigationStack with MonarchStepper, the step's content and a bottom bar of MonarchButton Back and Continue; interactiveDismissDisabled once the person has started
summary: A recipe, not a component: a task of a few steps in a sheet, with a stepper showing progress, the current step's content, Back and Continue, and a danger last step.
whenToUse: For a short task with two to five ordered steps that belongs over the current screen: setting up an integration, moving a project, deleting a workspace with checks.
whenNotToUse: For one step use a sheet (see responsive-dialog). For a long onboarding flow use pushed screens in a NavigationStack. For a form whose steps are independent, use one scrolling form with sections.
api: MonarchStepper.init(_ steps: [MonarchStepperStep], current: Int, furthest: Int? = nil, orientation: MonarchStepperOrientation = .horizontal, compact: MonarchStepperCompactMode = .automatic, labels: MonarchStepperLabels = MonarchStepperLabels(), onSelect: (@MainActor (MonarchStepperStep, Int) -> Void)? = nil)
func sheet(isPresented: Binding<Bool>, content: () -> some View) -> some View
func interactiveDismissDisabled(_ isDisabled: Bool = true) -> some View
MonarchButton.init(_ title: String, …, variant: MonarchButtonVariant = .secondary, …, action: @escaping @MainActor () -> Void)

states.name: step
states.description: The stepper marks the current step; the content shows the step's title (a header) and fields; Back and Continue are at the bottom.

states.name: blocked
states.description: Continue is disabled while the step is not valid, with the reason shown as caption text next to the buttons.

states.name: destructive last step
states.description: Continue is named after the action ("Delete workspace") and uses the danger variant.

states.name: started
states.description: After the first step the sheet cannot be swiped away; Cancel in the toolbar closes it.

appearance: A system sheet on the theme's surface colour with MonarchStepper (accent for the current step), Monarch text styles, a secondary Back button and a primary or danger Continue button.
platformNotes: The web WizardDialog is a component that takes steps with content, canContinue, blockedReason, a per-step async onContinue with pending and error states, and a done step. On iOS the app holds the step index and composes MonarchStepper and MonarchButton in a sheet; a step's async work uses the button's isLoading and shows failures with MonarchInlineNotice. The web moves focus to the step heading; on iOS post an AccessibilityNotification.Announcement of the new step or use AccessibilityFocusState. Android plans the same recipe.
accessibility: MonarchStepper reads "Step 2 of 4" and each step's state; the step title has the header trait.
Announce the new step with AccessibilityNotification.Announcement when Continue or Back changes it, since focus stays on the button.
A disabled Continue has its reason shown as text, not only a dimmed button.
Cancel is in the toolbar with the cancellationAction placement, so the escape gesture is not the only way out once dismissal is disabled.
edgeCases: At compact widths the stepper switches to its compact form by itself.
Keep the entered values in the parent's state so Back shows them again.
Reset the step to the first when the sheet is dismissed.
